findings.snippet: _SHOW_ROW_CAP = 10_000  # Snowflake caps SHOW output at this many rows and does not flag the truncation.
findings.fix_hint: No true fix is available: SHOW OPENFLOW DEPLOYMENTS/RUNTIMES/CONNECTORS is a Snowflake-side command with no cursor or LIMIT/OFFSET parameter, so this source cannot page past the row cap the way the ACCOUNT_USAGE history queries do. The scal-001 fix (_warn_if_show_truncated) converts a silent truncation into a detected, counted, warned one, which is the correct mitigation given the platform constraint. Left open only because the underlying platform limitation is not something this connector's code can close; re-evaluate if Snowflake ever adds a cursor to the OPENFLOW SHOW commands.

notes: Full 10-row rubric re-run from scratch against snowflake_openflow.py + snowflake_openflow_{config,models,query,report}.py only, per scope restriction.

Row 1 (cursor pagination): ACCOUNT_USAGE history queries (deployment/runtime/connector_history) use manual CREATED_ON cursor with LIMIT, inclusive `>=` boundary, and stall/NULL-cursor guards (_paged_history) -- compliant. SHOW OPENFLOW ... has no pagination primitive at all (platform limitation, not a code defect) -- residual gap tracked as scal-003 (Low).

Row 2 (workunit streaming): get_workunits_internal is a generator yielding per-deployment/runtime/connector/table-job. The three _fetch_* methods and the paged-history accumulator materialize bounded lists, which _PLANNING.md's performance section explicitly documents and justifies as deliberate (merge_show_and_history needs both SHOW and history sides in hand; the runtime-key map must reflect only containers actually emitted this run). No hidden or surprise materialization found.

Row 3 (SQL query-log LIMIT+cursor): N/A -- USAGE_STATS is declined (capability_matrix.USAGE_STATS = no); OPENFLOW_USAGE_HISTORY reports Snowflake credit consumption, not dataset usage, and is not queried by this connector at all.

Row 4 (SqlParsingAggregator): N/A -- lineage_strategy.approach = custom-upstream. No SQL is parsed; edges are built directly from connector configuration key-value pairs (parse_connector_config). Explicitly justified in _PLANNING.md: 'SqlParsingAggregator would have nothing to consume.'

Row 5 (memory profile vs planning): _PLANNING.md performance.memory_profile explicitly documents three bounded accumulators (paged history rows, merged object sets, and get_workunits_internal's deployments/runtimes/by_deployment_name/runtime_keys_by_name). Verified these are the only such accumulators in get_workunits_internal and _fetch_inventory; no undocumented dict[urn, full_schema]-style accumulator found. Compliant with the documented intent.

Row 6 (bounded concurrency): N/A -- no ThreadPoolExecutor or asyncio usage anywhere in scope (grep confirmed zero hits). Concurrency is declared sequential by design in _PLANNING.md, with a stated future trigger (see scal-004) for revisiting.

Row 7 (connection pooling): Compliant -- a single SnowflakeConnection is created once in __init__ (self.connection = config.connection.get_connection()) and reused for every query and every stage GET; closed once in close(). No per-call connection or engine creation found (grep for requests.get/post and create_engine returned zero hits, as expected for a Snowflake-connector-based source).

Row 8 (retry policy): Compliant and verified fixed this round -- see scal-005 resolution above. Retries are exponential-backoff (tenacity Retrying, multiplier configurable for tests, max 4s cap, 3 attempts), gated to a narrow set of transient/connection-class exceptions, applied at exactly one layer per call site. The SDK-client retry/endpoint-override sub-checks under Row 8 are N/A: this connector does not wrap a shared vendor SDK client/session factory (no .client(/.stub(/.channel( construction sites); it uses the family's existing SnowflakeConnection directly.

Row 9 (per-entity-type counts): Compliant -- SnowflakeOpenflowReport tracks num_deployments, num_runtimes, num_connectors, num_table_jobs, num_lineage_edges, num_owners_emitted, plus numerous skip/drop/failure counters per category, giving operators granular progress and failure visibility.

Row 10 (N+1): No SQL-form N+1 (not a SQLAlchemy/inspector-based source). API-form N+1 exists (one stage GET per connector for config-derived lineage, one DESCRIBE per distinct runtime for the external URL) and is already an accepted, documented, capped architectural decision -- see scal-004 (Low, carried forward, now additionally surfaced in operator-facing docs).

source_type_classification rationale: this connector queries Snowflake via SnowflakeConnection with hand-written SQL/SHOW/DESCRIBE/GET statements against ACCOUNT_USAGE views and stage files -- closest to the sql_warehouse classification even though it is not a SQLAlchemy table/column extractor. Rows 2, 5 and 9 (the embedded/API-agnostic rows) were evaluated as first-class regardless of classification.

No new Critical, High, or Medium findings identified in this fresh full-rubric pass. Both findings carried forward from the previous round (scal-003, scal-004) are Low and represent platform limitations / already-documented, capped architectural trade-offs rather than code defects.
